To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
RARγ1 controls a switch between differentiation and apoptosis in SK-N-B2(c) neuroblatoma cells.
in SK-N-BEE neuroblastoma cells, RARγ controls RARβ expression and that the reciprocal expression of RARs is involved in the control of cell proliferation and cell differentiation.
in neuroblastoma cells, RA receptor γ1 acts as a negative regulator of RA receptor β2 expression and controls a differentiation-apoptotic switch.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of retinoic acid receptor expression and its effects on cell proliferation and differentiation.
the role of retinoids in the development of the nervous system.
understanding the molecular mechanism by which RARγ1 regulates RARβ expression in SK-N-B2(c) cells and the role of these RARs in controlling cell proliferation and differentiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the expression of RAREs in neuroblastoma cell lines is regulated in such a way that it can be used as a marker for the differentiation status and that the RARs are able to regulate a differentiation-apoptotic switch in neuroblastoma cells.
RA regulates the expression of Rarβ2 via a negative feedback loop that involves Rarγ1.
RARγ1 controls RARβ2 expression in SK-N-B2(c) neuroblatoma cells and regulates a differentiation-apoptotic switch.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
RARγ1 levels are a critical determinant of the response of neuroblastoma cells and other RA-sensitive cell types to RA.
RARγ1 levels regulate the balance between proliferation and differentiation in neuroblastoma cells, and that this is achieved by reciprocal regulation of RARβ expression.
the expression levels of RARγ are important for the control of cell proliferation, differentiation, and apoptosis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
RARγ1 can act as a transcriptional repressor in the absence of RA and as a transcriptional activator in its presence, thus controlling the expression of RARB2 in SK-N-B2(c) cells.

the expression level of the RA receptor RARγ1 controls the expression of another RA receptor RARβ2 in SK-N-BEC neuroblastoma cells and regulates the balance between proliferation and apoptosis in these cells.

reciprocal regulation of expression and function of the RAR isoforms may be an important component of the regulation of the effects of retinoids on cell proliferation and differentiation in the developing nervous system.
